[← Back to the lesson: Computational complexity of LLMs](../llm-computational-complexity.qmd)

## Check your understanding

1. **Dense attention is quadratic: why can it still be computed in parallel?** Interactions between positions are parallelizable matrix operations; total work and sequential depth are different.

   <details>
   <summary>Worked answer</summary>

   Scores for all pairs of positions can be computed as the matrix operation $QK^\top$, and the resulting weights multiply $V$. Positions therefore need not be processed one after another within the layer. Total work remains quadratic in sequence length, but hardware parallelism reduces the sequential depth of the computation.

   </details>
2. **Why is standard generation still sequential?** The next token depends on the token just selected.

   <details>
   <summary>Worked answer</summary>

   Autoregressive generation must wait for the token selected at the previous step: that token becomes part of the context that determines the next distribution. The initial prompt can be processed in parallel during prefill; decode steps for one sequence, however, depend on one another.

   </details>
3. **Does FlashAttention make attention linear?** No: it retains quadratic work while reducing memory movement and intermediates.

   <details>
   <summary>Worked answer</summary>

   FlashAttention does not remove interactions between token pairs: dense attention still has quadratic work in sequence length. Its contribution is algorithmic and hardware-aware: tiled computation reduces memory traffic and avoids materializing the full attention matrix in GPU high-bandwidth memory.

   </details>
4. **Is a recurrent model with linear work in $T$ fully parallel?** No: a naïve recurrence depends on the previous state, although some structures enable parallel scans.

   <details>
   <summary>Worked answer</summary>

   A general recurrence imposes the dependency $h_t=f(h_{t-1},x_t)$: state $t$ must wait for state $t-1$. Work can be linear in $T$ while sequential depth is also linear. Parallel scans are available for associative operations or specially structured recurrences; this does not make every arbitrary recurrence parallelizable.

   </details>
5. **Does an MoE with few active experts store only those experts?** No: all expert weights must be hosted or accessible.

   <details>
   <summary>Worked answer</summary>

   Sparse routing limits the computation for one token to its $k$ selected experts, reducing active parameters and FLOPs per token. But the weights of all experts remain model parameters: they must be stored in memory or made accessible, possibly through distribution or offloading. Active parameters and total storage capacity are different quantities.

   </details>
